The difference between disabled and readonly is that read-only controls can still be interacted + with and submitted, whereas disabled controls are entirely non-interactive. What "interactive"
body: Thanks for writing this up—I think it is a big improvement in clarity though IMHO “entirely non-interactive” is still overstating things—and maybe emphasizing “interaction” is not ideal. So as an alternative I think it could be better to describe it in terms of _function_—with a reference to the normative requirements at that point—so that the above would become something like this: > read-only controls can still function (cause data to be submitted, or cause the state of the application to change, etc.) whereas disabled controls cannot usefully function at all as controls (cannot cause data to be submitted, and cannot cause the state of the application to change, etc.). For details about the normative requirements, see the section on the `disabled` concept (which defines requirements for the `activation behavior` and of a disabled control, and for whether or not it is a `focusable area`). And then for the next part of the Note, maybe something more like this: > However, except for than the functional/focusable behavior, any other behavior related to user interaction with disabled controls (for example, whether text of the control can be selected or copied) is a user-interface decision left up to the user agent. However, I don’t feel strongly about those changes being necessary (this is still just a Note…) so if you believe that what you already have in this change is good, I’m totally fine with with it being merged as-is.
